standard.title: Plan and transact with others
standard.description: participate in activities that involve planning and transacting with others, using a range of phrases, structures and modelled sentences in familiar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges, collaborate in play-based activities, and use digital formats for interaction (AC9LCH4C01, AC9LCH2C02). They can take turns, give instructions and participate in role-play. They have not yet participated in transactional exchanges (buying, ordering, negotiating), planned and presented cultural items, or interacted with guest speakers in structured contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in activities that involve planning and transacting with others — including role-plays involving transactions, planning and presenting cultural performances, and interacting with guests — using a range of phrases, structures and modelled sentences.

nodes.label: Transactional role-play language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in transactional role-plays — buying, ordering, negotiating — using appropriate request forms, quantity and price language, and transaction-closing expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one transactional role-play (e.g. buying food, ordering a meal) using at least three appropriate target language phrases for the transaction.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in transactional scenarios — shops, restaurants, markets — making requests, stating preferences, negotiating quantity and price, and concluding transactions; use appropriate modelled language for different stages of a transaction; use real or simulated currency or props.
wider: Compare how transactions are conducted in the target language community with Australian conventions — identify differences in etiquette, bargaining norms, or interaction patterns
Extend a transactional role-play beyond a scripted exchange — add complications (wrong item, price disagreement, special request) and negotiate a resolution
nodes.hinge_reason: Transactional language is the functional prerequisite for all planning and negotiation activity. Students who cannot manage a basic transaction cannot participate in the more complex planning and collaborative presentation tasks this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Transactional language transfers across different transaction types — food ordering, shopping, seeking services. Practising across varied scenarios (not only one scripted shop) builds the flexible transactional capacity that the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Participates in a transactional role-play using at least three appropriate target language phrases
Successfully completes a transaction — stating a preference, negotiating or requesting, and closing the exchange

nodes.label: Planning and presenting cultural items
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and present a cultural item — a performance, cultural display, or community event contribution — collaborating with peers and using appropriate target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to planning and presenting at least one cultural item (performance, display, or presentation) using at least four target language phrases appropriate to the task.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and present cultural items — reciting poems, singing songs, performing dances, creating cultural displays — for school or community audiences; collaborate in group planning and decision-making; follow procedures and give instructions in the target language.
wider: Lead or coordinate a cultural presentation — making decisions about content, assigning roles, and directing the group using target language
Compare how the cultural item is presented to different audiences (classmates, families, community members) and adapt language and format accordingly

response_modes.reason: Planning and presenting integrates transactional and collaborative language skills into a sustained, purposeful activity with a real audience. The teaching investment is in supporting genuine collaboration — not only rehearsed performance — where students negotiate roles, content and decisions in the target language.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cultural performance and presentation tasks draw on background learners' authentic cultural knowledge and community connections. Width investment here — real audiences, real cultural content — creates the highest-authenticity condition for target language use at this level.
success_criteria: Contributes to planning and presenting a cultural item using at least four target language phrases
Collaborates with peers in at least one planning decision — role allocation, content choice, or task assignment

nodes.label: Interacting with guests and in community contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interact with guest speakers or classroom visitors using appropriate target language, and adapt their language to the context of the interaction.
nodes.minimum_width: Interact with at least one guest speaker or visitor using at least two appropriate target language phrases — for example, a greeting, a question, or an expression of thanks.
nodes.typical_width: Interact with guest speakers, community visitors, or participants in special occasions using appropriate language; adapt language to context and relationship; work in teams to create collaborative digital resources or activities for sharing with others.
wider: Prepare questions in advance for a guest speaker, conduct the interaction, and report back to peers on what was learned
Compare how interaction with a guest speaker differs from peer interaction — what changes in language, register, and manner, and why

response_modes.reason: Interaction with guests requires explicit preparation — students need to understand what makes this interaction context different from peer exchange, and to prepare appropriately. Structured preparation tasks (generating questions, practising register-appropriate greetings) support confident participation.

success_criteria: Interacts with a guest or visitor using at least two appropriate target language phrases
Adapts language or manner to the guest context — for example, using more formal address or prepared questions
